old_row.rationale: The departure of fearful men resembles Judas's earlier dismissal of the fearful according to the law, but this account characterizes their departure as distrust rather than repeating that legal procedure.

proposed_new_row.rationale: The departure of fearful men resembles the companion account's dismissal of the fearful according to the law, but this account characterizes their departure as distrust rather than repeating that legal procedure.

required_changes.issue: The word 'earlier' adds a chronological relation between the two narrated departures that neither passage establishes. Both passages occur in preparation for the Nicanor/Gorgias campaign; 1 Maccabees 3:56 is in the Emmaus preparation, not an explicitly earlier dismissal within 2 Maccabees' chronology.
required_changes.required_action: Replace 'Judas's earlier dismissal of the fearful according to the law' with 'the companion account's dismissal of the fearful according to the law'. Retain the target, relationship, and contrast between legal dismissal and distrust.

precision_notes: All 294 actual source units were personally read before any author packet was bound. Complete triple displays then supplied every retained source, full target range, relationship and rationale; displays were not truncated.
Nanea death, failed Elymais raid, and chapter 9 illness remain separate unresolved candidates with zero credit. The name Antiochus is not used to force a single death sequence.
Apollonius Thraseas/Menestheus and Joseph/John discrepancies remain unresolved. Neither Jonathan in the opening liturgy nor Eleazar the martyr is assigned an identity from shared names.

The opening letters and Chislev Booths-style purification festival are distinguished from ordinary Booths and from the separate Nehemiah fire tradition. Moses/Solomon passages support the particular cloud, fire, sin-offering, and dedication claims.
Greek source numbering has been directly read at Leviticus 5:21-24, Exodus 22:6-8 and 22:21-23, and Psalms 19:8; no familiar numbering was substituted.

Cross-book campaign comparisons preserve troop figures, casualties, commands, timing notices, and officer titles. The Beth-horon speech at 1 Maccabees 3:18-21 is used only as a comparable exhortation, not identified as the Nicanor battle.

Hebrews 11:35 comparisons retain thematic similarity without identifying its unnamed sufferers as Eleazar, the mother, or individual brothers. Creation and resurrection comparisons state their shared claims without importing absent details.
All same-chapter connections were personally assessed for an express correction, command/answer, repetition, reversal, appointment/abuse, or narrative recap and carry the required same-chapter label.
All 100 source-only deferrals were personally reread with their complete source bodies and reasons; they remain zero credit and do not become completed merely because a source unit has been read.
All four candidate complete triples and the stated surrounding contexts were personally read; all remain unresolved, unretained, and zero credit.
